# app-tokens create

Command: `boundary app-tokens create`

The `app-tokens create` command lets you create Boundary app
token resources.

## Examples

The following example creates an app token by passing in a scope and permissions. You can pass permissions directly
as a JSON array or as a path to a JSON file using the file:// prefix, for example, `file://perms.json`.

```shell-session
$ boundary app-tokens create \
  -scope-id $SCOPE_ID \
  -name "Example App Token" \
  -description "An example app token in the global scope." \
  -time-to-live 30d \
  -time-to-stale 1d \
  -permissions '[{"grants":["id=*;type=target;actions=list,read"],"grant_scopes":["this"]}]'
```

**Example output:**

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```plaintext
App Token information:
  Approximate Last Access Time:   Thu, 01 Oct 2026 18:04:09 PDT
  Created By User ID:             u_1234567890
  Created Time:                   Thu, 01 Oct 2026 18:04:09 PDT
  Description:                    An example app token in the global scope.
  Expiration Time:                Sat, 31 Oct 2026 18:04:09 PDT
  ID:                             appt_1234567890
  Name:                           Example App Token
  Status:                         active
  Token:
  appt_0123456789_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz1234567890abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz1234567890abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz1234567890

  Scope:
    ID:                           global
    Name:                         global
    Type:                         global

  Permissions:
    Permission 1:
      Grants:
        id=*;type=target;actions=list,read
      Grant Scopes:
        this

  Authorized Actions:

    no-op
    read
    read:self
    revoke
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

Copy the app token's `token` value in the response. This is the only time the app token's `token` value is displayed. You will not 
have another opportunity to save it.

## Usage

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```shell-session
$ boundary app-tokens create [options] [args]
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

### Command options

- `-description` `(string: "")` - The description to set on the app token.
- `-name` `(string: "")` - The name to set on the app token.
- `-scope-id` `(string: "")` - The scope in which to make the request. You can also 
    specify the scope using the **BOUNDARY_SCOPE_ID** environment variable.
- `-time-to-live` `(string: "")` - The duration of the app token. Passed in as a duration
    string (uses d, h, m, s, ms, ns as options).
- `-time-to-stale` `(string: "")` - The optional duration of inactivity after which 
    the token becomes stale. Passed in as a duration string (uses d, h, m, s, ms, ns as options).
- `-permissions` `(string: "")` - The permissions to set for the
    app token. Can be passed directly as a JSON array (for example `'[{"grants":["id=*;type=target;actions=list,read"],"grant_scopes":["this"]}]'`) or as
    a path to a JSON file using the file:// prefix (for example `file://perms.json`).
